subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 47-year-old man with major depressive disorder and diabetic neuropathy is started on duloxetine. His physician wants an agent that acts on both serotonin and norepinephrine pathways.
question: What is the mechanism of action of duloxetine?

options.text: Selective inhibition of 5-HT reuptake
Inhibition of both 5-HT and norepinephrine reuptake
Nonselective inhibition of monoamine oxidase
Antagonism of alpha-2 adrenergic autoreceptors
Direct agonism at 5-HT1A receptors

explanation_correct: SNRIs such as duloxetine inhibit reuptake of both 5-HT and norepinephrine, increasing levels of both neurotransmitters. This dual action underlies their efficacy in depression, anxiety disorders, and painful conditions such as diabetic neuropathy. It is the defining mechanistic distinction from the SSRIs.

explanation_incorrect.A: Selective 5-HT reuptake inhibition is the SSRI mechanism.
explanation_incorrect.C: Monoamine oxidase inhibition is the MAOI mechanism.
explanation_incorrect.D: Alpha-2 autoreceptor antagonism is the mechanism of mirtazapine.
explanation_incorrect.E: 5-HT1A receptor agonism is the mechanism of buspirone.

educationalObjective: SNRIs inhibit reuptake of both serotonin and norepinephrine.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A physician is matching individual SNRIs to their specific approved indications. She wants to select one SNRI for a patient with fibromyalgia and another for a patient with social anxiety disorder.
question: Which pairing of SNRI and indication is correct?

options.text: Duloxetine — fibromyalgia; venlafaxine — social anxiety disorder
Venlafaxine — fibromyalgia; duloxetine — social anxiety disorder
Milnacipran — diabetic neuropathy only; venlafaxine — fibromyalgia
Desvenlafaxine — panic disorder; milnacipran — obsessive-compulsive disorder
Levomilnacipran — post-traumatic stress disorder; venlafaxine — fibromyalgia

explanation_correct: Duloxetine and milnacipran are indicated for fibromyalgia, whereas venlafaxine is additionally indicated for social anxiety disorder, panic disorder, PTSD, and OCD. As a class, SNRIs also treat depression, generalized anxiety disorder, and diabetic neuropathy. These drug-specific indications are frequently tested.

explanation_incorrect.B: Venlafaxine is not a fibromyalgia agent; duloxetine is the SNRI used for fibromyalgia.
explanation_incorrect.C: Milnacipran is used for fibromyalgia, and venlafaxine is not indicated for fibromyalgia.
explanation_incorrect.D: The high-yield pairing is venlafaxine for panic disorder and OCD, not desvenlafaxine and milnacipran in these roles.
explanation_incorrect.E: Venlafaxine, not levomilnacipran, is associated with PTSD, and venlafaxine is not used for fibromyalgia.

educationalObjective: Duloxetine and milnacipran are used for fibromyalgia, whereas venlafaxine covers social anxiety, panic, PTSD, and OCD.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A 50-year-old man with depression and hypertension is started on venlafaxine. At follow-up his blood pressure has risen and he reports persistent nausea.
question: Which set of adverse effects is most consistent with SNRI therapy?

options.text: Tremor, hypothyroidism, and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus
Postural hypotension, dry mouth, and urinary retention
Hypertensive crisis after ingestion of tyramine-containing foods
Marked sedation, weight gain, and no cardiovascular effects
Increased blood pressure, stimulant effects, sedation, sexual dysfunction, and nausea

explanation_correct: SNRIs can increase blood pressure and produce stimulant effects, sedation, sexual dysfunction, and nausea. The elevation in blood pressure is an important consideration in patients with preexisting hypertension. This side-effect profile stems from enhanced noradrenergic transmission combined with serotonergic effects.

explanation_incorrect.A: Tremor, hypothyroidism, and nephrogenic diabetes insipidus are lithium adverse effects.
explanation_incorrect.B: Postural hypotension and anticholinergic effects such as dry mouth and urinary retention are TCA effects.
explanation_incorrect.C: Tyramine-induced hypertensive crisis is a concern with MAOIs, not SNRIs.
explanation_incorrect.D: SNRIs can raise blood pressure and are not free of cardiovascular effects.

educationalObjective: SNRIs can increase blood pressure and cause stimulant effects, sedation, sexual dysfunction, and nausea.

subject: Psychiatry
vignette: A student reviewing antidepressant classes wants to identify the group of drugs that are SNRIs.
question: Which of the following groups consists entirely of SNRIs?

options.text: Fluoxetine, sertraline, citalopram
Amitriptyline, imipramine, clomipramine
Venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, levomilnacipran, milnacipran
Phenelzine, selegiline, isocarboxazid
Buspirone, mirtazapine, bupropion

explanation_correct: Venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, levomilnacipran, and milnacipran are SNRIs that inhibit reuptake of both 5-HT and norepinephrine. Memorizing the drug names within this class allows rapid prediction of their shared mechanism and adverse-effect profile.

explanation_incorrect.A: Fluoxetine, sertraline, and citalopram are SSRIs.
explanation_incorrect.B: Amitriptyline, imipramine, and clomipramine are tricyclic antidepressants.
explanation_incorrect.D: Phenelzine, selegiline, and isocarboxazid are monoamine oxidase inhibitors.
explanation_incorrect.E: Buspirone, mirtazapine, and bupropion are not SNRIs.

educationalObjective: The SNRIs include venlafaxine, desvenlafaxine, duloxetine, levomilnacipran, and milnacipran.
